sanskrit: yasmin vinaṣṭe pāñcālāḥ saha putrais tathā vayam sātyakir vāsudevaś ca vinaśyeyur asaṃśayam
english: If he were lost, the Pāñcālas with their sons, and we ourselves, and Sātyaki and Vāsudeva — all would perish without doubt.

sanskrit: yo 'sau gacchati tejasvī bahūn kleśān acintayan bhavanniyogād bībhatsus tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim
english: That radiant one goes, ignoring countless hardships, by your command — Arjuna does so; what then is more painful than this?

sanskrit: yasya bāhū samāśritya vayaṃ sarve mahātmanaḥ manyāmahe jitān ājau parān prāptāṃ ca medinīm
english: Relying on whose arms we all consider the foes already defeated in battle and the earth already won.

sanskrit: yasya prabhāvān na mayā sabhāmadhye dhanuṣmataḥ nītā lokam amuṃ sarve dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ sasaubalāḥ
english: Because of whose power I did not send all the Dhārtarāṣṭras together with Subala's son to the other world in the midst of the assembly hall, though he was armed with his bow.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ bāhubalinaḥ krodham utthitam ātmanaḥ sahāmahe bhavanmūlaṃ vāsudevena pālitāḥ
english: We, endowed with the strength of our arms, endure the anger rising within us — anger rooted in your decision — while being protected by Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: vayaṃ hi saha kṛṣṇena hatvā karṇamukhān parān svabāhuvijitāṃ kṛtsnāṃ praśāsema vasuṃdharām
english: For we, together with Kṛṣṇa, having slain the enemies headed by Karṇa, could rule the entire earth conquered by our own arms.

sanskrit: bhavato dyūtadoṣeṇa sarve vayam upaplutāḥ ahīnapauruṣā rājan balibhir balavattamāḥ
english: By the fault of your dice-playing we are all overwhelmed — we whose valor is undiminished, O king, who are mightier than the mighty.

sanskrit: kṣātraṃ dharmaṃ mahārāja samavekṣitum arhasi na hi dharmo mahārāja kṣatriyasya vanāśrayaḥ rājyam eva paraṃ dharmaṃ kṣatriyasya vidur budhāḥ
english: You ought to consider the duty of a warrior, great king; for dwelling in the forest is not the dharma of a kṣatriya, great king — the wise know that sovereignty alone is the highest dharma of a kṣatriya.

sanskrit: sa kṣatradharmavid rājan mā dharmyān nīnaśaḥ pathaḥ prāg dvādaśa samā rājan dhārtarāṣṭrān nihanmahi
english: You who know the warrior's dharma, O king — do not stray from the righteous path. Before the twelve years are up, O king, let us slay the Dhārtarāṣṭras.

sanskrit: nivartya ca vanāt pārtham ānāyya ca janārdanam vyūḍhānīkān mahārāja javenaiva mahāhave dhārtarāṣṭrān amuṃ lokaṃ gamayāmi viśāṃ pate
english: Calling back Pārtha from his quest and summoning Janārdana, great king, I will swiftly dispatch the Dhārtarāṣṭras with their arrayed forces to the other world in great battle, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: sarvān ahaṃ haniṣyāmi dhārtarāṣṭrān sasaubalān duryodhanaṃ ca karṇaṃ ca yo vānyaḥ pratiyotsyate
english: I shall slay all the Dhārtarāṣṭras together with Subala's son, Duryodhana and Karṇa, and whoever else shall oppose us in battle.

sanskrit: mayā praśamite paścāt tvam eṣyasi vanāt punaḥ evaṃ kṛte na te doṣo bhaviṣyati viśāṃ pate
english: After I have pacified them you can return from the forest. If done this way, no fault will attach to you, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: yajñaiś ca vividhais tāta kṛtaṃ pāpam ariṃdama avadhūya mahārāja gacchema svargam uttamam
english: And having shaken off the sin committed through various sacrifices, O subduer of enemies, O great king, we can go to the highest heaven.

sanskrit: evam etad bhaved rājan yadi rājā na bāliśaḥ asmākaṃ dīrghasūtraḥ syād bhavān dharmaparāyaṇaḥ
english: This could indeed be so, O king, if the king were not foolish; but you are one who procrastinates for us, O you who are devoted to dharma.

sanskrit: nikṛtyā nikṛtiprajñā hantavyā iti niścayaḥ na hi naikṛtikaṃ hatvā nikṛtyā pāpam ucyate
english: It is settled that the deceitful, whose intelligence is deceit, must be slain by deceit; for slaying the treacherous by treachery is not called a sin.

sanskrit: tathā bhārata dharmeṣu dharmajñair iha dṛśyate ahorātraṃ mahārāja tulyaṃ saṃvatsareṇa hi
english: So too in matters of dharma it is seen by those who know dharma, O Bhārata — a single day and night, great king, is equal to a full year.

sanskrit: tathaiva vedavacanaṃ śrūyate nityadā vibho saṃvatsaro mahārāja pūrṇo bhavati kṛcchrataḥ
english: And likewise the Vedic word is heard always, O lord — a year, O great king, becomes complete through difficulty.

sanskrit: yadi vedāḥ pramāṇaṃ te divasād ūrdhvam acyuta trayodaśa samāḥ kālo jñāyatāṃ pariniṣṭhitaḥ
english: If the Vedas are your authority, O unfailing one, reckoning beyond the single day — the time of thirteen years is to be understood as fully elapsed.

sanskrit: kālo duryodhanaṃ hantuṃ sānubandham ariṃdama ekāgrāṃ pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ purā rājan karoti saḥ
english: The time has come to slay Duryodhana together with his followers, O subduer of foes — lest he make the entire earth under one sole rule first, O king.

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ bhīmaṃ tu dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ uvāca sāntvayan rājā mūrdhny upāghrāya pāṇḍavam
english: While Bhīma was speaking thus, King Yudhiṣṭhira, the dharma-king, addressed him soothingly, smelling the Pāṇḍava's head.

sanskrit: asaṃśayaṃ mahābāho haniṣyasi suyodhanam varṣāt trayodaśād ūrdhvaṃ saha gāṇḍīvadhanvanā
english: Without doubt, O mighty-armed one, you will slay Suyodhana after the thirteenth year is past, together with the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva bow.

sanskrit: yac ca mā bhāṣase pārtha prāptaḥ kāla iti prabho anṛtaṃ notsahe vaktuṃ na hy etan mayi vidyate
english: And what you say to me — "the time has come, O lord" — I cannot bring myself to speak an untruth; for this is not in me.

sanskrit: antareṇāpi kaunteya nikṛtiṃ pāpaniścayam hantā tvam asi durdharṣa sānubandhaṃ suyodhanam
english: Even without resorting to treachery or evil resolve, O son of Kuntī, you shall be the slayer of Suyodhana and his followers, O invincible one.

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvati bhīmaṃ tu dharmarāje yudhiṣṭhire ājagāma mahābhāgo bṛhadaśvo mahān ṛṣiḥ
english: While king Yudhiṣṭhira, the dharma-king, was speaking thus to Bhīma, the great and fortunate sage Bṛhadaśva arrived.

sanskrit: tam abhiprekṣya dharmātmā saṃprāptaṃ dharmacāriṇam śāstravan madhuparkeṇa pūjayām āsa dharmarāṭ
english: Beholding him who had arrived — the righteous one who walks in dharma — the dharma-souled king of righteousness honored him according to the scriptures with the madhuparka offering.

sanskrit: āśvastaṃ cainam āsīnam upāsīno yudhiṣṭhiraḥ abhiprekṣya mahābāhuḥ kṛpaṇaṃ bahv abhāṣata
english: When he was seated at ease, Yudhiṣṭhira, the mighty-armed, sitting near him and beholding him, spoke many words piteously.

sanskrit: akṣadyūtena bhagavan dhanaṃ rājyaṃ ca me hṛtam āhūya nikṛtiprajñaiḥ kitavair akṣakovidaiḥ
english: By dice-play, O blessed one, my wealth and kingdom have been taken from me — having been summoned and cheated by deceitful gamblers who were skilled at dice.

sanskrit: anakṣajñasya hi sato nikṛtyā pāpaniścayaiḥ bhāryā ca me sabhāṃ nītā prāṇebhyo 'pi garīyasī
english: I, knowing nothing of dice, was cheated by those of evil resolve — and my wife, dearer to me than life itself, was dragged into the assembly hall.

sanskrit: asti rājā mayā kaś cid alpabhāgyataro bhuvi bhavatā dṛṣṭapūrvo vā śrutapūrvo 'pi vā bhavet na matto duḥkhitataraḥ pumān astīti me matiḥ
english: Is there any king more unfortunate than I on this earth — one seen by you before, or even heard of before? It is my belief that there is no man more miserable than I.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca yad bravīṣi mahārāja na matto vidyate kva cit alpabhāgyataraḥ kaś cit pumān astīti pāṇḍava
english: Bṛhadaśva said: What you say, great king, that nowhere is there any man more unfortunate than I — hear this, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: atra te kathayiṣyāmi yadi śuśrūṣase 'nagha yas tvatto duḥkhitataro rājāsīt pṛthivīpate
english: I shall tell you of this, if you wish to hear, O sinless one — there was a king more miserable than you, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca athainam abravīd rājā bravītu bhagavān iti imām avasthāṃ saṃprāptaṃ śrotum icchāmi pārthivam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the king said to him, "Let the blessed one speak" — I wish to hear of the king who has come to such a condition.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca śṛṇu rājann avahitaḥ saha bhrātṛbhir acyuta yas tvatto duḥkhitataro rājāsīt pṛthivīpate
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Listen attentively, O king, together with your brothers, O steadfast one — there was a king more miserable than you, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: niṣadheṣu mahīpālo vīrasena iti sma ha tasya putro 'bhavan nāmnā nalo dharmārthadarśivān
english: There was a king of the earth among the Niṣadhas known as Vīrasena; his son was named Nala, who was versed in dharma and the goals of life.

sanskrit: sa nikṛtyā jito rājā puṣkareṇeti naḥ śrutam vanavāsam aduḥkhārho bhāryayā nyavasat saha
english: That king was defeated by deceit — by Puṣkara, as we have heard — and though undeserving of such hardship, he dwelt in the forest with his wife.

sanskrit: na tasyāśvo na ca ratho na bhrātā na ca bāndhavāḥ vane nivasato rājañ śiṣyante sma kadā cana
english: For that king dwelling in the forest, O king, neither horse, nor chariot, nor brother, nor kinsman ever remained with him.

sanskrit: bhavān hi saṃvṛto vīrair bhrātṛbhir devasaṃmitaiḥ brahmakalpair dvijāgryaiś ca tasmān nārhasi śocitum
english: But you are surrounded by heroic brothers equal to the gods, and by foremost twice-born ones who are like Brahmā — therefore you ought not to grieve.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca vistareṇāham icchāmi nalasya sumahātmanaḥ caritaṃ vadatāṃ śreṣṭha tan mamākhyātum arhasi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I wish to hear at length, O best among speakers, the story of the great-souled Nala — please narrate it to me.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca āsīd rājā nalo nāma vīrasenasuto balī upapanno guṇair iṣṭai rūpavān aśvakovidaḥ
english: Bṛhadaśva said: There was a king named Nala, the powerful son of Vīrasena, endowed with desired virtues, handsome, and skilled in the knowledge of horses.

sanskrit: atiṣṭhan manujendrāṇāṃ mūrdhni devapatir yathā upary upari sarveṣām āditya iva tejasā
english: He stood at the head of human kings as the lord of the gods stands above all — above all others, like the sun in radiance.

sanskrit: brahmaṇyo vedavic chūro niṣadheṣu mahīpatiḥ akṣapriyaḥ satyavādī mahān akṣauhiṇīpatiḥ
english: Devoted to the Brahmins, learned in the Vedas, heroic, the great lord of the earth among the Niṣadhas, fond of dice, truthful in speech, the great commander of armies.

sanskrit: īpsito varanārīṇām udāraḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ rakṣitā dhanvināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ sākṣād iva manuḥ svayam
english: Desired by the best of women, generous, with controlled senses, a protector, the foremost of archers — like Manu himself in person.

sanskrit: tathaivāsīd vidarbheṣu bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ śūraḥ sarvaguṇair yuktaḥ prajākāmaḥ sa cāprajaḥ
english: And likewise among the Vidarbhas there was Bhīma of terrible valor, a hero endowed with all virtues, who desired offspring but had none.

sanskrit: sa prajārthe paraṃ yatnam akarot susamāhitaḥ tam abhyagacchad brahmarṣir damano nāma bhārata
english: He made supreme effort, well-composed in mind, for the sake of offspring; and the brahmarṣi named Damana came to him, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: taṃ sa bhīmaḥ prajākāmas toṣayām āsa dharmavit mahiṣyā saha rājendra satkāreṇa suvarcasam
english: Bhīma who desired offspring — knowing dharma — gratified that lustrous one together with his queen, O lord of kings, with reverent hospitality.

sanskrit: tasmai prasanno damanaḥ sabhāryāya varaṃ dadau kanyāratnaṃ kumārāṃś ca trīn udārān mahāyaśāḥ
english: Pleased with him, the greatly famous Damana granted a boon to him and his wife — a jewel of a daughter and three noble, greatly glorious sons.

sanskrit: damayantīṃ damaṃ dāntaṃ damanaṃ ca suvarcasam upapannān guṇaiḥ sarvair bhīmān bhīmaparākramān
english: Damayantī, Dama, Dānta, and Damana of fine radiance — all endowed with every virtue, formidable as Bhīma, of terrible valor.

sanskrit: damayantī tu rūpeṇa tejasā yaśasā śriyā saubhāgyena ca lokeṣu yaśaḥ prāpa sumadhyame
english: But Damayantī, the slender-waisted one, gained fame in the worlds through her beauty, splendor, renown, fortune, and good fortune.

sanskrit: atha tāṃ vayasi prāpte dāsīnāṃ samalaṃkṛtam śataṃ sakhīnāṃ ca tathā paryupāste śacīm iva
english: When she came of age, a hundred well-adorned maidservants and companions waited upon her as upon Śacī herself.

sanskrit: tatra sma bhrājate bhaimī sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā sakhīmadhye 'navadyāṅgī vidyut saudāminī yathā atīva rūpasaṃpannā śrīr ivāyatalocanā
english: There the daughter of Bhīma — adorned with all ornaments, her limbs beyond reproach — shone among her companions like a flash of lightning, exceedingly endowed with beauty, like Śrī herself with wide eyes.

sanskrit: na deveṣu na yakṣeṣu tādṛg rūpavatī kva cit mānuṣeṣv api cānyeṣu dṛṣṭapūrvā na ca śrutā cittapramāthinī bālā devānām api sundarī
english: Nowhere among gods, nor among yakṣas, nor among other humans, had such a beautiful woman been seen before or even heard of — the young girl who confounded the mind, beautiful even to the gods.

sanskrit: nalaś ca naraśārdūlo rūpeṇāpratimo bhuvi kandarpa iva rūpeṇa mūrtimān abhavat svayam
english: And Nala, the tiger among men, was unequaled on earth in beauty — like the god of love embodied in form itself.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ samīpe tu nalaṃ praśaśaṃsuḥ kutūhalāt naiṣadhasya samīpe tu damayantīṃ punaḥ punaḥ
english: In her presence they praised Nala out of curiosity, and in the presence of the Niṣādha king they praised Damayantī again and again.

sanskrit: tayor adṛṣṭakāmo 'bhūc chṛṇvatoḥ satataṃ guṇān anyonyaṃ prati kaunteya sa vyavardhata hṛcchayaḥ
english: Love arose between the two of them who constantly heard each other's virtues without having seen each other, O son of Kuntī — and that longing of the heart kept growing toward each other.

sanskrit: aśaknuvan nalaḥ kāmaṃ tadā dhārayituṃ hṛdā antaḥpurasamīpasthe vana āste rahogataḥ
english: Unable to bear the love in his heart, Nala then stayed alone in the garden near the inner apartments.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa tadā haṃsāñ jātarūpaparicchadān vane vicaratāṃ teṣām ekaṃ jagrāha pakṣiṇam
english: He then saw geese with golden-colored plumage wandering in the garden; of those birds he caught one.

sanskrit: tato 'ntarikṣago vācaṃ vyājahāra tadā nalam na hantavyo 'smi te rājan kariṣyāmi hi te priyam
english: Then that sky-traveler spoke to Nala: "I am not to be killed by you, O king — for I shall do you a favor."

sanskrit: damayantīsakāśe tvāṃ kathayiṣyāmi naiṣadha yathā tvad anyaṃ puruṣaṃ na sā maṃsyati karhi cit
english: "I shall speak of you in the presence of Damayantī, O king of the Niṣadhas — such that she will never think of any man other than you."

sanskrit: evam uktas tato haṃsam utsasarja mahīpatiḥ te tu haṃsāḥ samutpatya vidarbhān agamaṃs tataḥ
english: Addressed thus, the lord of the earth then released the goose. And those geese flew up and went from there to Vidarbha.

sanskrit: vidarbhanagarīṃ gatvā damayantyās tadāntike nipetus te garutmantaḥ sā dadarśātha tān khagān
english: Having gone to the city of Vidarbha, the winged ones alighted near Damayantī; and she then saw those birds.

sanskrit: sā tān adbhutarūpān vai dṛṣṭvā sakhigaṇāvṛtā hṛṣṭā grahītuṃ khagamāṃs tvaramāṇopacakrame
english: Seeing those birds of wondrous form, surrounded by her group of companions, she joyfully and eagerly set about to catch the birds.

sanskrit: atha haṃsā visasṛpuḥ sarvataḥ pramadāvane ekaikaśas tataḥ kanyās tān haṃsān samupādravan
english: Then the geese scattered in all directions through the ladies' garden; and then the maidens each chased after those geese one by one.

sanskrit: damayantī tu yaṃ haṃsaṃ samupādhāvad antike sa mānuṣīṃ giraṃ kṛtvā damayantīm athābravīt
english: But the goose that Damayantī ran after close at hand — that one, adopting a human voice, then spoke to Damayantī:

sanskrit: damayanti nalo nāma niṣadheṣu mahīpatiḥ aśvinoḥ sadṛśo rūpe na samās tasya mānuṣāḥ
english: "Damayantī, there is a king named Nala, lord of the earth among the Niṣadhas, equal to the Aśvins in beauty — no humans are equal to him."

sanskrit: tasya vai yadi bhāryā tvaṃ bhavethā varavarṇini saphalaṃ te bhavej janma rūpaṃ cedaṃ sumadhyame
english: "If you were to become his wife, O fair-complexioned one, your birth would be fruitful and this beauty of yours, O slender-waisted one."

sanskrit: vayaṃ hi devagandharvamanuṣyoragarākṣasān dṛṣṭavanto na cāsmābhir dṛṣṭapūrvas tathāvidhaḥ
english: "For we have seen gods, gandharvas, humans, serpents, and rākṣasas — and yet one such as him has never been seen by us before."

sanskrit: tvaṃ cāpi ratnaṃ nārīṇāṃ nareṣu ca nalo varaḥ viśiṣṭāyā viśiṣṭena saṃgamo guṇavān bhavet
english: "And you are a jewel among women, and Nala is the best among men — the union of the excellent with the excellent would be full of virtue."

sanskrit: evam uktā tu haṃsena damayantī viśāṃ pate abravīt tatra taṃ haṃsaṃ tam apy evaṃ nalaṃ vada
english: Thus addressed by the goose, Damayantī, O lord of the people, said to that goose there: "Say the same to Nala as well."

sanskrit: tathety uktvāṇḍajaḥ kanyāṃ vaidarbhasya viśāṃ pate punar āgamya niṣadhān nale sarvaṃ nyavedayat
english: The bird, having said "So be it" to the daughter of the lord of Vidarbha, O lord of the people, came back again to the Niṣādha country and reported everything to Nala.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca damayantī tu tac chrutvā vaco haṃsasya bhārata tadā prabhṛti nasvasthā nalaṃ prati babhūva sā
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Damayantī, having heard that word of the goose, O Bhārata, from that time onward became unsettled in mind regarding Nala.

sanskrit: tataś cintāparā dīnā vivarṇavadanā kṛśā babhūva damayantī tu niḥśvāsaparamā tadā
english: Then Damayantī became absorbed in thought, wretched, pale-faced, thin, constantly sighing at that time.

sanskrit: ūrdhvadṛṣṭir dhyānaparā babhūvonmattadarśanā na śayyāsanabhogeṣu ratiṃ vindati karhi cit
english: With upward gaze, absorbed in meditation, she appeared as one deranged — never finding pleasure in bed, seat, or enjoyment at any time.

sanskrit: na naktaṃ na divā śete hā heti vadatī muhuḥ tām asvasthāṃ tadākārāṃ sakhyas tā jajñur iṅgitaiḥ
english: She slept neither by night nor by day, saying "Alas! Alas!" again and again; and her companions recognized her unsettled state and such condition through signs.

sanskrit: tato vidarbhapataye damayantyāḥ sakhīgaṇaḥ nyavedayata nasvasthāṃ damayantīṃ nareśvara
english: Then the group of Damayantī's companions reported to the lord of Vidarbha that Damayantī was not herself, O lord of men.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā nṛpatir bhīmo damayantīsakhīgaṇāt cintayām āsa tat kāryaṃ sumahat svāṃ sutāṃ prati
english: Hearing that from Damayantī's group of companions, king Bhīma reflected deeply on that very great matter concerning his own daughter.

sanskrit: sa samīkṣya mahīpālaḥ svāṃ sutāṃ prāptayauvanām apaśyad ātmanaḥ kāryaṃ damayantyāḥ svayaṃvaram
english: The lord of the earth, observing his own daughter who had reached the bloom of youth, saw that the proper course of action for him was Damayantī's svayaṃvara.

sanskrit: sa saṃnipātayām āsa mahīpālān viśāṃ pate anubhūyatām ayaṃ vīrāḥ svayaṃvara iti prabho
english: He summoned the lords of the earth, O lord of the people: "Let this svayaṃvara be attended, O heroes, O lords" — so said he.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu pārthivāḥ sarve damayantyāḥ svayaṃvaram abhijagmus tadā bhīmaṃ rājāno bhīmaśāsanāt
english: Hearing of Damayantī's svayaṃvara, all the kings then came to Bhīma, those rulers summoned by Bhīma's command.

sanskrit: hastyaśvarathaghoṣeṇa nādayanto vasuṃdharām vicitramālyābharaṇair balair dṛśyaiḥ svalaṃkṛtaiḥ
english: Making the earth resound with the noise of elephants, horses, and chariots, with their forces well-adorned with varied garlands and ornaments and fine to behold.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu purāṇāv ṛṣisattamau aṭamānau mahātmānāv indralokam ito gatau
english: At this very time two ancient foremost sages, the great-souled wanderers, departed from here and went to Indra's world.
